Analysis.object: For disordered eating, category prediction accuracy based on psychological resilience, circus factors and demographics was estimated to be approximately 69%. Trait resilience was associated with decreased likelihood of being at risk of an eating disorder. Modality of engagement in circus was not associated with disordered eating. Of the demographic factors, only age was associated with eating disorders.

The circus-specific exercise addiction questionnaire demonstrated low reliability, thereby potentially attenuating the correlations between this variable and the model predictors. Self report natures of screening tool

We recommaled future research adopts a longitudinal study design to allow for assessment of patterns of emergence of disordered eating and exercise addictions. Ths could also shed light into the question whether disordered eating or exercise addiction emerge first among those circus artists who experience both mental health problemes.

Population.object: Circus artists ranged from 18 to 69 years of age
Amateur level (n=248), part-time professional circus artists (n=140), full-time professional (n=64), full-time students at national circus schools (n=31), retired circus artists (n=17)
